**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either:
• the color of the top discard card,
• the number/symbol of the top discard card,
• or a Wild card (any color).
After playing, the card’s effect (if any) takes place immediately. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you can be challenged.) | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise your turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip, Reverse, Draw Two = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Game End** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon score (usually 500) wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on the discard pile** – you can often anticipate what cards opponents might play. 2. **Use Wild Draw Four wisely** – it’s powerful but risky if you’re caught. 3. **Plan your “UNO”** – keep track of when you’ll be the last card so you can shout it in time. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
